name: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI Compute)
what_it_is: Enterprise cloud VMs notable for a generous Always Free ARM Ampere A1 tier (up to 4 OCPUs and 24 GB RAM).
programmable_control: CLI (`oci compute instance launch/get/action/terminate`) and OCI REST API — https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/api/#/en/iaas/
auth_method: RSA API signing key pair (`~/.oci/config`) or instance principals
usage_or_limits: OCI Limits API (`oci limits value list`) and Usage API (`oci usage-api usage-summary request-summarized-usages`)
pricing_model: Always Free tier: 2 AMD micro VMs + up to 4 Ampere A1 ARM OCPUs & 24 GB RAM (1-4 VMs) forever; pay-as-you-go beyond free caps
os_platforms: Linux (x86_64, ARM64 Ampere) and Windows VMs; `oci` CLI cross-platform
fit_reason: Unbeatable Always Free 4-core/24GB ARM tier for personal fleets, though RSA key setup and capacity availability add friction.

name: OVHcloud Public Cloud
what_it_is: OpenStack-based European public cloud offering Linux/Windows VMs, GPUs, and managed Kubernetes with zero internal egress fees.
open_source: No (proprietary cloud built on OpenStack; `ovhcloud` CLI open-source)
programmable_control: CLI (`ovhcloud`), OVHcloud REST API (`/cloud/project/{id}/instance`), and standard OpenStack APIs — https://api.ovh.com
auth_method: OVH API consumer key / OAuth2 / OpenStack credentials
usage_or_limits: Billing usage endpoint `GET /cloud/project/{id}/usage/current` and OpenStack quota API
pricing_model: No permanent free tier; hourly or monthly billing with 15-30% savings plans; local storage and IPv4 billed separately
os_platforms: Linux, Windows, and GPU VMs across EU/CA/US/APAC
fit_reason: Strong EU data-sovereignty option with OpenStack compatibility and usage API, though more complex setup than Hetzner.

name: UpCloud
what_it_is: High-IOPS MaxIOPS cloud servers with a clean HTTPS REST v1.3 API and `upctl` Go CLI.
programmable_control: CLI (`upctl server create/show/stop/delete`) and REST API (`https://api.upcloud.com/1.3/server`) — https://upcloud.com/docs/guides/upcloud-api/
auth_method: Bearer API token (`UPCLOUD_TOKEN` or `upctl account login --with-token`)
usage_or_limits: Account endpoint `GET /1.3/account` returns credits and resource limits
pricing_model: No always-free tier (trial credits available); hourly/monthly server plans starting ~$3-5/mo
os_platforms: Linux and Windows VMs across EU/US/APAC; `upctl` cross-platform
fit_reason: Clean Bearer-token API and `upctl` CLI with built-in account credits/limits endpoint.

name: Exoscale
what_it_is: Swiss/European sovereign cloud VMs, SKS Kubernetes, and GPU nodes with per-second billing and open-source `exo` CLI.
programmable_control: CLI (`exo compute instance create/show/stop/delete`) and REST API v2 — https://openapi-v2.exoscale.com/
auth_method: HMAC API key + secret (`EXOSCALE_API_KEY`, `EXOSCALE_API_SECRET`)
usage_or_limits: Quotas via `exo limits` / `GET /v2/quota`
pricing_model: No free tier; per-second billing from ~EUR 5.32/mo (1 vCPU / 0.5 GB RAM) with 1 TiB/mo egress bundled per instance
os_platforms: Linux and Windows VMs in Swiss/EU zones; `exo` CLI cross-platform
fit_reason: Strong Swiss/EU compliance and clean `exo` CLI with per-second billing and quota reads.

name: RunPod
what_it_is: Per-second GPU Pods (Secure Cloud & Community Cloud) and Serverless GPU workers for AI workloads and local-model agents.
programmable_control: REST API v2 (`https://api.runpod.io/v2`), GraphQL API, and `runpodctl` CLI (`runpodctl create/stop/remove pod`) — https://docs.runpod.io
auth_method: API key (`RUNPOD_API_KEY`)
usage_or_limits: Account balance and active pods readable via RunPod GraphQL/REST API
pricing_model: No free tier; prepaid credits, per-second GPU billing (RTX 4090 from ~$0.34 Community / $0.89 Secure; H100 ~$1.99-$3.99/hr) + $0.10/GB-mo volume storage
os_platforms: Linux Docker GPU containers (NVIDIA); CLI/API cross-platform
fit_reason: Fast per-second GPU pods for GPU-heavy or self-hosted-model agent tickets, though overkill for CPU coding fleets.

name: Vast.ai
what_it_is: P2P GPU compute marketplace offering low-cost on-demand and interruptible Docker GPU instances.
programmable_control: CLI (`vastai search offers`, `vastai create instance`, `vastai show instances`, `vastai stop/destroy instance`) and REST API (`/api/v0/`) — https://vast.ai/docs
auth_method: API key (`vastai set api-key`)
usage_or_limits: CLI `vastai show user` and `/api/v0/users/current/` return live credit balance
pricing_model: No free tier; market-driven per-second GPU rates (often lowest on market); allocated disk bills even while stopped
os_platforms: Linux Docker GPU containers on community/datacenter hosts; CLI cross-platform
fit_reason: Cheapest raw GPU compute, but variable third-party host reliability and trust model make it risky for private repos.

name: Lambda Cloud
what_it_is: On-demand single-GPU VMs and multi-node H100/B200 clusters with zero data egress fees.
programmable_control: Cloud REST API (`POST /api/v1/instance-operations/launch`, `GET /api/v1/instances`, `POST /api/v1/instance-operations/terminate`) — https://docs.lambdalabs.com/api/cloud
auth_method: Bearer API key
usage_or_limits: Instance types/availability endpoint `GET /api/v1/instance-types`; programmatic billing balance endpoint unverified
pricing_model: No free tier; hourly pay-as-you-go (A6000 ~$0.92/hr, A100 ~$1.48+/hr, H100 ~$2.86-$3.78/hr, B200 ~$6.08/hr) with $0 egress
os_platforms: Ubuntu Linux GPU VMs
fit_reason: Clean REST API and zero egress fees for GPU-bound ML tickets, though capacity fluctuates and no small CPU tier exists.

name: NVIDIA Brev
what_it_is: Multi-cloud developer GPU environment launcher with a single `brev` CLI aggregating AWS, GCP, Lambda, Nebius, and others.
programmable_control: CLI (`brev login`, `brev create`, `brev shell`, `brev stop`, `brev delete`) — https://docs.nvidia.com/brev/
auth_method: CLI OAuth (`brev login`)
usage_or_limits: CLI `brev ls` lists active instances; programmatic billing API unverified
pricing_model: No permanent free tier; per-second pass-through GPU rates based on selected cloud provider/instance
os_platforms: Linux GPU dev VMs; `brev` CLI on macOS and Linux
fit_reason: Super simple `brev` CLI for GPU devboxes across clouds, tailored specifically to GPU/CUDA workflows.

name: Nebius AI Cloud
what_it_is: AI-native cloud providing per-second NVIDIA H100/B200/B300 VMs, Managed Kubernetes, and Token Factory model inference.
programmable_control: Nebius CLI (`nebius`), REST/gRPC APIs, and Go/Python/JS SDKs for compute VMs and K8s — https://docs.nebius.com
auth_method: IAM token / OAuth (`nebius iam`) / service account keys
usage_or_limits: CLI/API exposes spot pricing history, quotas, and billing data — https://docs.nebius.com
pricing_model: No permanent free tier; per-second GPU/CPU billing (H100 on-demand ~$4.50/hr, spot lower; B300 ~$9.50/hr)
os_platforms: Linux CPU/GPU VMs and Managed Kubernetes
fit_reason: Strong enterprise GPU/K8s APIs plus model hosting, best for AI/ML-heavy fleets.

name: CoreWeave
what_it_is: Kubernetes-native bare-metal GPU cloud built for large-scale AI training and inference clusters with zero egress fees.
open_source: No (proprietary cloud running standard Kubernetes API)
programmable_control: Standard Kubernetes API (`kubectl` / client-go / Python K8s client on CoreWeave Kubernetes Service) — https://docs.coreweave.com
auth_method: Kubeconfig / OIDC / CoreWeave IAM token
usage_or_limits: Kubernetes ResourceQuota + CoreWeave telemetry/billing console (programmatic billing endpoint unverified)
pricing_model: No free tier; node/8-GPU cluster hourly rates (L40 ~$1.25/GPU-hr, A100 ~$2.70, H100 ~$6.16, B200 ~$8.60); Spot/Reserved up to 60% off; free egress
os_platforms: Linux bare-metal GPU Kubernetes nodes
fit_reason: Cluster-scale 8-GPU nodes are built for large training runs rather than single-ticket coding builders; already reachable via Kubernetes driver.

name: Tart
what_it_is: Apple Virtualization.framework CLI for running OCI-distributed macOS and Linux VMs on Apple Silicon Macs (with Orchard cluster API).
open_source: Source-available (FSL-1.1-ALv2 at github.com/openai/tart, converts to Apache-2.0 after 2 years)
programmable_control: CLI (`tart clone`, `tart run`, `tart ip`, `tart exec`, `tart list`, `tart stop`, `tart delete`) and Orchard cluster REST API — https://tart.run/quick-start/
auth_method: Local macOS user (or Orchard API token / OCI registry credentials)
usage_or_limits: Local Mac host hardware limits (Apple EULA caps 2 concurrent macOS VMs per Mac host); `tart list` shows state
pricing_model: Free for internal/non-competitive use under FSL-1.1-ALv2; pay only your Apple Silicon hardware
os_platforms: macOS Apple Silicon hosts running macOS and Linux ARM64 guest VMs
fit_reason: Best self-hosted macOS VM runner for Apple Silicon iOS/macOS coding agents with clean `tart` CLI and OCI golden images.

name: MacStadium Orka
what_it_is: Managed Kubernetes-native macOS virtualization control plane hosted on dedicated Apple Silicon Mac hardware.
programmable_control: CLI (`orka3` / `orka` v4: `orka vm deploy/list/delete`) and Orka REST API — https://orkadocs.macstadium.com
auth_method: Orka API token / SSO login (`orka login`)
usage_or_limits: Cluster node/VM resource visibility via `orka` CLI and REST API
pricing_model: No free tier; dedicated hosted Mac servers from ~$109-$449+/mo per physical Mac node
os_platforms: macOS Apple Silicon VMs on hosted Mac mini / Mac Studio clusters
fit_reason: Enterprise-grade API-controlled macOS VMs for iOS/macOS builds, though high dedicated-hardware floor limits casual use.

name: Docker Engine
what_it_is: Ubiquitous Linux OCI container engine runnable locally or on any remote VPS over Unix socket, SSH, or TLS TCP.
open_source: Yes (Apache-2.0 at github.com/moby/moby; Docker Desktop commercial subscription required for large enterprises)
programmable_control: CLI (`docker run -d`, `docker exec`, `docker inspect`, `docker stop`, `docker rm`) and Docker Engine HTTP API (`/containers/create`, `/start`, `/exec`, `/stop`) — https://docs.docker.com/reference/api/engine/
auth_method: Local Unix socket / SSH context (`DOCKER_HOST=ssh://...`) / mTLS certificates
usage_or_limits: CLI `docker stats --no-stream`, `docker system df`, and Engine API `GET /containers/{id}/stats`
pricing_model: Free open-source on Linux (Apache-2.0); Docker Desktop free for personal/small business (<250 employees and <$10M revenue), paid Pro/Team/Business otherwise
os_platforms: Linux native; macOS and Windows via VM (Docker Desktop, Colima, OrbStack)
fit_reason: Universal zero-vendor-lock-in container isolation on laptops and VPSes, though shared-kernel isolation is weaker than microVMs.

name: Docker Sandboxes (sbx)
what_it_is: MicroVM-backed sandboxes (`sbx` CLI) built specifically for running Claude Code, Codex, and other coding agents safely locally or on Docker cloud.
open_source: No (proprietary Docker CLI/platform; local use free)
programmable_control: CLI (`sbx create`, `sbx run`, `sbx ls`, `sbx stop`, `sbx rm --force`) — https://docs.docker.com/ai/sandboxes/
auth_method: None for local microVMs; Docker account login for cloud compute & Agentic Platform policies
usage_or_limits: CLI `sbx ls` for active/stopped sandboxes; cloud usage limits via Docker Agentic Platform (programmatic API unverified)
pricing_model: Local microVM sandboxes and `sbx` CLI are free including commercial use; Docker-managed cloud compute & org governance require paid Docker Agentic Platform + usage
os_platforms: Linux microVM guests on macOS, Windows, and Linux hosts (plus Docker cloud)
fit_reason: Free local hardware-isolated microVMs tailored to coding agents with Docker-in-sandbox and clean `sbx` lifecycle commands.

name: Kubernetes
what_it_is: Industry-standard container orchestration control plane running ephemeral Jobs or stateful Pods across any cloud or on-prem cluster.
programmable_control: CLI (`kubectl apply`, `kubectl exec`, `kubectl get pods/jobs`, `kubectl delete`) and Kubernetes REST API (`/apis/batch/v1/namespaces/{ns}/jobs`, `/api/v1/.../pods`) — https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/kubernetes-api/
auth_method: Kubeconfig (OIDC, client certs, service account tokens, cloud IAM)
usage_or_limits: Kubernetes ResourceQuota API (`kubectl describe quota`), Metrics Server (`kubectl top pod`), and cluster autoscaler metrics
pricing_model: Free open-source (Apache-2.0); pay only underlying cluster/managed K8s (EKS/GKE/AKS/Hetzner/bare metal)
os_platforms: Linux (x86_64, ARM64) and Windows worker nodes; `kubectl` cross-platform
fit_reason: Every large org already operates Kubernetes; pairing with Kata/gVisor RuntimeClass gives strong fleet isolation at scale.

name: Kubernetes Agent Sandbox
what_it_is: Official Kubernetes SIG Apps declarative `Sandbox` CRD and controller for isolated, stateful singleton agent runtimes over gVisor or Kata.
programmable_control: Kubernetes CRD API (`kubectl apply/get/delete sandbox`, warm pools, pause/resume) — https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox
auth_method: Kubernetes RBAC / kubeconfig / service account tokens
usage_or_limits: Kubernetes ResourceQuota, LimitRange, and Metrics APIs
pricing_model: Free open-source (Apache-2.0); runs on any Kubernetes cluster
os_platforms: Linux Kubernetes pods with gVisor or Kata Containers isolation
fit_reason: Standardizes warm pools and stateful singleton agent sandboxes directly inside Kubernetes without custom pod-lifecycle glue.

name: Podman
what_it_is: Daemonless, rootless OCI container engine with a Docker-compatible CLI and REST API.
programmable_control: CLI (`podman run -d`, `podman exec`, `podman inspect`, `podman stop`, `podman rm`) and libpod/Docker-compatible REST API — https://docs.podman.io
auth_method: Local rootless user / SSH remote connections (`podman --remote`)
usage_or_limits: CLI `podman stats --no-stream` and `podman system df`
pricing_model: Free open-source (Apache-2.0) on all platforms including commercial desktop use
os_platforms: Linux native; macOS and Windows via built-in `podman machine` Linux VM
fit_reason: Rootless daemonless drop-in alternative to Docker without Docker Desktop licensing restrictions.

name: Microsandbox
what_it_is: Open-source self-hosted microVM runtime (`msb` CLI + SDKs) using KVM/Hypervisor.framework/WHP to boot OCI images in ~100-200ms.
programmable_control: CLI (`msb create`, `msb run`, `msb stop`), Rust/Python/TS/Go SDKs, and MCP server — https://github.com/superradcompany/microsandbox
auth_method: Local server / configurable API key
usage_or_limits: Local host CPU/RAM limits; `msb` status commands
pricing_model: Free open-source (Apache-2.0); self-hosted on your own laptop or server
os_platforms: macOS (Apple Silicon), Linux (KVM), Windows (WHP)
fit_reason: Cross-platform Apache-2.0 microVMs with sub-200ms OCI boot and no Docker daemon — strong local/self-hosted isolation.

name: BoxLite
what_it_is: Daemonless, embeddable open-source microVM engine (`boxlite`) running persistent OCI images with `allow_net` egress and host-proxy secret injection.
programmable_control: Python/Node/Rust library (`boxlite.SimpleBox(image=...)`, `box.exec(...)`, optional server mode) — https://github.com/boxlite-ai/boxlite
auth_method: Local embedded process (no daemon/root required)
usage_or_limits: Local host CPU/RAM bounds; per-box resource limits configurable in SDK
pricing_model: Free open-source (Apache-2.0)
os_platforms: macOS (Apple Silicon) and Linux (KVM) hosts running Linux OCI microVMs
fit_reason: Embeddable Apache-2.0 microVM with host-proxy secret injection and persistent turns matches OpenWiz security philosophy closely.

name: Apple Container
what_it_is: Apple open-source CLI (`container`) running each Linux OCI container inside its own lightweight Apple Silicon microVM.
programmable_control: CLI (`container run`, `container exec`, `container ls`, `container stop`, `container rm`) and macOS XPC API (`container-apiserver`) — https://github.com/apple/container
auth_method: Local macOS user
usage_or_limits: Local Mac CPU/RAM limits; `container ls` for running VMs
pricing_model: Free open-source (Apache-2.0)
os_platforms: macOS 26+ on Apple Silicon running Linux ARM64 microVM containers
fit_reason: First-party Apple microVM-per-container isolation on modern Macs with zero third-party desktop daemon.

name: Firecracker
what_it_is: Minimalist Rust KVM virtual machine monitor powering AWS Lambda, Fargate, E2B, and Fly microVMs with ~125ms boot.
programmable_control: Unix-socket HTTP REST API (`PUT /boot-source`, `PUT /drives/{id}`, `PUT /actions` InstanceStart/SendCtrlAltDel, `PUT /snapshot/create`) — https://github.com/firecracker-microvm/firecracker/blob/main/docs/api_requests/actions.md
auth_method: Local Unix socket permissions (Linux host with `/dev/kvm`)
usage_or_limits: Local host KVM resources; `/metrics` FIFO for VM telemetry
pricing_model: Free open-source (Apache-2.0); runs on bare-metal Linux or nested-KVM cloud hosts
os_platforms: Linux x86_64 and ARM64 hosts with KVM
openwiz_plug_in: driver (low-level substrate; prefer wrapper like E2B/Incus/Microsandbox)
fit_reason: Gold-standard microVM VMM, but raw Firecracker lacks rootfs/image/network management so higher-level wrappers are faster to ship.

name: Kata Containers
what_it_is: Open-source OCI runtime that runs standard containers inside lightweight hardware-virtualized VMs (QEMU, Cloud Hypervisor, Firecracker).
programmable_control: Plugs into containerd/CRI-O/Kubernetes via `runtimeClassName: kata` or `ctr run --runtime io.containerd.kata.v2` — https://github.com/kata-containers/kata-containers/tree/main/docs
auth_method: Inherits host containerd/Kubernetes RBAC
usage_or_limits: Inherits Kubernetes/containerd resource quotas and cgroup metrics
pricing_model: Free open-source (Apache-2.0)
os_platforms: Linux hosts with hardware virtualization (x86_64, ARM64, s390x, ppc64le)
openwiz_plug_in: driver (via Kubernetes or containerd runtime class)
fit_reason: Hardens Kubernetes and containerd fleets to VM-level isolation without changing the OpenWiz driver API.

name: gVisor
what_it_is: User-space application kernel (`runsc`) providing an OCI container sandbox boundary without requiring nested KVM.
programmable_control: OCI runtime via Docker (`docker run --runtime=runsc`) or Kubernetes (`runtimeClassName: gvisor`) — https://gvisor.dev/docs/
auth_method: Inherits Docker/Kubernetes host permissions
usage_or_limits: Inherits Docker/Kubernetes resource limits and `runsc metric-export`
pricing_model: Free open-source (Apache-2.0)
os_platforms: Linux x86_64 and ARM64 (works even on cloud VMs without nested virtualization)
fit_reason: Trivially upgrades any Docker/K8s VPS (even without KVM) to strong syscall isolation via a single `--runtime=runsc` flag.

name: Incus
what_it_is: Community-maintained successor to LXD managing full Linux system containers and QEMU VMs across single hosts or clusters.
programmable_control: CLI (`incus launch --vm`, `incus exec`, `incus list`, `incus stop`, `incus delete`, `incus snapshot`) and HTTPS/Unix-socket REST API (`/1.0/instances`) — https://linuxcontainers.org/incus/docs/main/
auth_method: Local Unix socket, TLS client certificates, or OIDC
usage_or_limits: Project quotas (`incus project info`), `incus info`, and Prometheus `/1.0/metrics` endpoint
pricing_model: Free open-source (Apache-2.0)
os_platforms: Linux hosts (x86_64, ARM64); `incus` remote CLI on macOS, Linux, Windows
fit_reason: Full Linux VMs + ZFS/Btrfs instant snapshots + clean REST API/CLI make Incus ideal for self-hosted bare-metal fleets.

name: Proxmox VE
what_it_is: Open-source KVM and LXC virtualization platform with clustering, ZFS snapshots, and a full REST API for homelabs and private datacenters.
open_source: Yes (AGPL-3.0; optional paid enterprise repository/support subscriptions)
programmable_control: REST API (`POST /api2/json/nodes/{node}/qemu/{vmid}/clone`, `.../status/start`, `.../status/stop`, `.../agent/exec`) and local CLI (`qm`, `pct`, `pvesh`) — https://pve.proxmox.com/pve-docs/api-viewer/
auth_method: PVE API token (`PVEAPIToken=user@realm!id=secret`) or PAM/OIDC ticket
usage_or_limits: Cluster resource & status endpoints (`GET /api2/json/cluster/resources`, `GET /api2/json/nodes/{node}/status`)
pricing_model: Free open-source (AGPL-3.0) with all features unlocked; optional support subscriptions per CPU socket/year
os_platforms: Debian Linux hypervisor running Linux, Windows, and BSD KVM VMs or LXC containers
fit_reason: Massive homelab and on-prem developer base; full clone/snapshot/agent-exec REST API fits OpenWiz cleanly.

name: HashiCorp Nomad
what_it_is: Lightweight workload orchestrator scheduling Docker, Podman, QEMU, Firecracker, and raw-exec batch jobs across clusters.
programmable_control: CLI (`nomad job run`, `nomad job status`, `nomad alloc exec`, `nomad job stop`, `-json`) and HTTP API (`/v1/jobs`, `/v1/allocation/{id}`) — https://developer.hashicorp.com/nomad/api-docs
auth_method: ACL Bearer token (`X-Nomad-Token`) or mTLS
usage_or_limits: Quota endpoints (`/v1/quotas`, `/v1/quota/usage/{name}`) and node stats (`/v1/client/stats`)
pricing_model: Free Community edition (BSL 1.1); paid Nomad Enterprise for namespaces/governance/quotas at scale
os_platforms: Linux, macOS, and Windows cluster nodes
fit_reason: Simpler than Kubernetes with native Docker/QEMU/exec drivers and quota APIs, though smaller footprint than K8s.

name: Lima
what_it_is: Open-source Linux VM manager (`limactl`) on macOS and Linux using Apple Virtualization.framework or QEMU with auto file/port sharing.
programmable_control: CLI (`limactl start`, `limactl shell`, `limactl list --json`, `limactl stop`, `limactl delete`, `limactl clone`) — https://lima-vm.io/docs/
auth_method: Local OS user (auto-managed SSH keys)
usage_or_limits: Local host CPU/RAM/disk bounds; `limactl list --json` reports VM allocations and status
pricing_model: Free open-source (Apache-2.0)
os_platforms: macOS (Apple Silicon & Intel) and Linux hosts running Linux guest VMs
fit_reason: Clean Apache-2.0 `limactl` CLI gives full isolated Linux VMs on macOS laptops with zero subscriptions.

name: OrbStack
what_it_is: Fast, lightweight macOS app and CLI (`orb`) for running Docker containers and full Linux VMs with minimal battery and RAM overhead.
programmable_control: CLI (`orb create`, `orb run -m <machine>`, `orb list`, `orb stop`, `orb delete`) plus Docker Engine API — https://docs.orbstack.dev/machines/commands
auth_method: Local macOS user
usage_or_limits: Local Mac CPU/RAM/disk bounds; `orb list` and `docker stats`
pricing_model: Free for personal non-commercial use; Pro/Business from $8/user/month ($96/yr) for commercial use
os_platforms: macOS hosts (Apple Silicon & Intel) running Linux machines and containers
fit_reason: Super popular among Mac developers with instant `orb create/run/stop/delete` Linux VMs and fast file sharing.

name: Colima
what_it_is: Open-source CLI providing container runtimes (Docker, containerd, Incus) inside Lima Linux VMs on macOS and Linux.
programmable_control: CLI (`colima start --profile`, `colima ssh`, `colima list --json`, `colima stop`, `colima delete`) plus Docker/Incus APIs — https://github.com/abiosoft/colima
auth_method: Local OS user
usage_or_limits: Local host hardware bounds; `colima list --json` shows profile CPU/memory/disk allocations
pricing_model: Free open-source (MIT)
os_platforms: macOS (Apple Silicon & Intel) and Linux hosts
openwiz_plug_in: driver (or backing VM for Docker/Incus drivers)
fit_reason: Free MIT runtime for Mac developers, though OpenWiz can target Docker/Incus/Lima directly without Colima-specific glue.

name: Canonical Multipass
what_it_is: Cross-platform CLI orchestrator launching on-demand Ubuntu cloud-init VMs locally on macOS, Linux, and Windows.
programmable_control: CLI (`multipass launch`, `multipass exec`, `multipass info --format json`, `multipass stop`, `multipass delete --purge`, `multipass snapshot`) — https://canonical.com/multipass/docs
auth_method: Local OS user (or authenticated remote client certificate)
usage_or_limits: Local host resources; `multipass info --format json` reports CPU/RAM/disk usage per VM
pricing_model: Free open-source (GPL-3.0)
os_platforms: macOS, Linux, and Windows hosts running Ubuntu Linux VMs
fit_reason: Clean cross-platform `multipass` CLI with built-in snapshots and cloud-init, though heavier boot than microVMs.

name: Local / SSH Host (OpenWiz Local Driver)
what_it_is: Runs coding-agent harnesses directly in isolated Git worktrees on your own Mac, Linux desktop, or persistent VPS with zero cloud sandbox fees.
programmable_control: OpenWiz driver v1 (`adapters/local/driver start`, `wake`, `stop`) using Linux subreaper or macOS process-group supervision — https://github.com/openwizdev/OpenWiz/tree/main/adapters/local
auth_method: Local OS logins (stays on your machine; `gh` + harness CLI logins)
usage_or_limits: Local machine CPU/RAM/disk (`os.cpu_count`, `df`)
pricing_model: Free open-source (Apache-2.0); zero extra compute cost beyond your own computer or VPS
os_platforms: macOS (Apple Silicon & Intel) and Linux
openwiz_plug_in: driver (existing verified OpenWiz driver in adapters/local)
fit_reason: Already passes OpenWiz driver v1 kit 5/5 with zero marginal compute cost and direct reuse of local harness logins.
